data.name: Nazariel
data.gender_notes: Nazariel is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Nazariel means 'God's helper'. This name is derived from the Hebrew word 'nazir', meaning 'consecrated' or 'set apart'. In the Bible, the name Nazariel appears in the Book of Tobit, where an angel named Raphael, which means 'God's healer', calls himself Nazariel when he appears in the guise of a human. As such, Nazariel is a name that signifies both divine assistance and divine healing.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name that signifies divine help and protection.
data.etymology: Nazariel belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “God's helper.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Nazariel total 5, giving a life-path number of 5. Number 5 is linked with Mercury and with the qualities of freedom, adaptability and curiosity.

in_hebrew.name: נצריאל
in_hebrew.long_meaning: נצריאל הוא שם יהודי ומשמעותו 'נצור' או 'איש האדון'. השם מופיע בברית החדשה באיסי 1:8–9. בתקופה הביזנטית, השם נחשב למיוחד ואומץ על ידי הנוצרים. בימי הביניים, השם נקשר לקבוצת הבני נצר.

in_greek.name: Ναζαριήλ
in_greek.long_meaning: Ὁ ὄνομα Ναζαριήλ ἐν τῇ Βίβλῳ προέρχεται ἀπὸ τῆς ἑβραϊκῆς λέξεως נצריאל. Ἐν τοῖς Ἀποστολικοῖς Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἔχει τὴν σημασίαν 'ἄνθρωπος τοῦ Κυρίου'. Ὁ Ναζαριήλ ἦν ἕνας τῶν Ἀποστόλων τοῦ Κυρίου. Ὁ ὄνομα Ναζαριήλ ἐν τῇ Ἐκκλησία τοῦ Θεοῦ ἐστὶ ὑπὲρ ἐξαίρετον καὶ θερμόν.

in_latin.name: Nazariel
in_latin.long_meaning: Nam Nazariel est nomen Hebraicum, quod significat 'servus' aut 'servus Domini'. In Novo Testamento, nomen Nazariel in Ioannis 1:8-9 mentionatur. In saeculis Byzantinis, nomen Nazariel erat nomen speciale et a Christianis adoptatum. In medio aevo, nomen Nazariel coniunctum est cum familia Nazarenorum.

in_english.name: Nazariel
in_english.meaning: of Nazareth origin, servant of the Lord
in_english.long_meaning: The name Nazariel originates from the Hebrew word נצריאל, meaning 'servant' or 'servant of the Lord.' In the New Testament, the name Nazariel appears in John 1:8-9. In the Byzantine era, the name Nazariel was considered unique and was adopted by Christians. In the Middle Ages, the name Nazariel was associated with the Nazarene family.

data.cultural_impact: The name Nazariel has a rich cultural significance in Jewish and Christian traditions. In Jewish tradition, the name is not commonly used, but it holds significance as the name of an angelic being who assisted Tobit in the Book of Tobit. In Christian tradition, the name Nazariel is less common but carries the meaning of God's helper and divine intervention.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Nazariel holds deep spiritual significance as it signifies the presence and intervention of God in one's life. It is a reminder that God is always with us and that we can call upon Him for assistance and healing. The name Nazariel can inspire faith, trust, and hope in God's divine providence and loving care. Additionally, the name can serve as a reminder of our own calling to be God's helpers and agents of healing in the world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Nazariel, in Hebrew meaning "God of Help," represents the divine assistance and protection granted by God during times of need and adversity. This name serves as a reminder of the strength and comfort one can find in their faith, particularly during challenging circumstances.

biblical_reference.note: The name Nazariel appears in the New Testament, specifically in John 1:8-9, referring to Jesus Christ.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Irenaeus of Lyon, Against Heresies, Book V, Chapter 21, Section 3 (circa 180 AD) The name Nazariel carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Irenaeus writes about the Archangels, including Nazariel, as part of a refutation of Gnostic heresies which denied the existence of the Creator God and the role of Christ in creation.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Pseudo-Dionysius the Areopagite, Celestial Hierarchy, Chapter 15 (circa 5th century AD) The name Nazariel carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: In this text, Nazariel is mentioned as one of the nine archangels who govern the seven heavens, but his role is not clearly defined.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Nazariel is rooted in Christian angelology and is sometimes used to refer to the archangel Raphael. In contemporary discussions, Nazariel is often mentioned in the context of spirituality and angelic protection. It can be found in various blog posts, books, and social media conversations about angelic guidance and healing. The name is also popular in fantasy literature, where it is used to depict powerful and benevolent angelic beings.
